title: The Design Challenge
summary: Separate requirements from preferences and begin a design with a clear problem and constraints.
objectives: Distinguish a requirement from a preference.
Use the define, require, constrain, design, test, improve process to frame a challenge.

vocab.def: Something a design must do or include.
A limit or condition a design must respect.
A planned solution to a problem.

sections.heading: Start with a real problem
sections.body: A community wants reliable digital services. The design must support computing, networks, power, cooling, security, and people. It also must respect community needs and available resources.

sections.heading: Requirements and preferences differ
sections.body: Reliable connectivity may be a requirement. A particular building color may be a preference. Naming the difference helps a team decide what cannot be left out.

sections.heading: Use the design cycle
sections.body: Define the problem, list what is required, identify constraints, choose a design, test what could fail, and improve it. There may be several reasonable designs.

practice.prompt: Classify each statement as a requirement or preference: reliable network service, a specific wall color, safe operation, and a particular logo.

quiz.question: What is a constraint?
options: A limit or condition a design must respect
quiz.answer: A limit or condition a design must respect

reflectionPrompt: Which requirement or constraint would be most important to your community design, and why?
